Minnesota's 15-game point streak ended Wednesday in a 4-3 loss to Utah that The Athletic called a rare sloppy effort, and Kirill Kaprizov's personal 15-game point streak ended with it. Before that night, Kaprizov had 23 points in 10 games against 15.1 our numbers expected. That is a superstar running hot, and both halves of the sentence matter.

The Wild are 18-4-5 with 41 points, and our simulations give them a 60% chance at the Central. The process is good: 56% of the expected goals overall (the quality of chances for and against), and the top line of Joel Eriksson Ek, Kaprizov and Matt Boldy has outscored teams 26-3 at 5v5. That number will not hold. Neither will the goaltending, which has stopped almost 14 more goals than expected, the main reason the record sits 6.5 points above what the chances earned.

Quinn Hughes is the other engine, with 16 points in 10 and a 12-3 goal margin beside Jared Spurgeon. He gave Minnesota a scare when he left a game after a collision with a Calgary forward, and his health is the one thing this team cannot replace.

The off-ice story is Bill Guerin's search for a center. After missing on Dylan Larkin, reports have linked the Wild to Boston's Pavel Zacha, Ryan O'Reilly and Evgeni Malkin. The second line of Yakov Trenin, Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov sits at 48% of the chances, which is why. What to watch: whether Guerin finds that center before the deadline.
headline: The streak ends, the center hunt doesn't
